review_notes: I read the whole file. I also grepped the sibling file OpenCohomologyPushforwardResolution.lean and Mathlib for an existing square-pasting lemma, and found none. Besides the finding below, I saw only small repetitions: the repeated `letI` PreservesZeroMorphisms/PreservesHomology blocks, and the `change` unfoldings. Those are routine unfolding, so I did not report them. I could not compile anything, so the shared lemma and rewrites below are sketches that have not been checked. The `_ ≫ _ ≫ _` association in the actual goals needs `Iso.trans_hom` and `Category.assoc` normalisation, and the `rfl` facts e₁/e₂ already provide that.

findings.problem: Both lemmas prove that a composite of isomorphisms is natural by pasting naturality squares. Each does this with the same hand-written `congrArg (fun k => … ≫ k)`/`Category.assoc` term chain, with `e₁ := rfl`/`e₂ := rfl` unfoldings and a final `refine … .trans` chain. The first lemma pastes three squares (h₁, h₂, h₃) through restated 5-fold composites (`h₂'`, `h₃'`, `h₁'`, `h₂''`). The second pastes two squares (h₁, h₂) through the same pattern (`h₂'`, `h₁'`). The same pasting argument therefore appears in two proofs, and in nested form inside the first one. Each statement is re-typed in full, with `presheafToSheaf … mapIso (HPrime…Iso …)` spelled out many times. This adds about 150 lines, hides the mathematical content (three squares paste), and makes any change to a comparison definition require editing many long terms.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one generic lemma in the category-theory section, for example:

`lemma paste_naturality_squares {C : Type*} [Category C] {A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂ D₁ D₂ : C} (u : A₁ ⟶ A₂) (v : B₁ ⟶ B₂) (w : D₁ ⟶ D₂) (e₁ : A₁ ⟶ B₁) (e₂ : A₂ ⟶ B₂) (g₁ : B₁ ⟶ D₁) (g₂ : B₂ ⟶ D₂) (h₁ : u ≫ e₂ = e₁ ≫ v) (h₂ : v ≫ g₂ = g₁ ≫ w) : u ≫ e₂ ≫ g₂ = (e₁ ≫ g₁) ≫ w`

Proof sketch: `rw [← Category.assoc, h₁, Category.assoc, h₂, Category.assoc]`, or `simp [reassoc_of% h₁, reassoc_of% h₂]`.

Rewrite the second lemma. Since `(…IsoRightDerivedObj f G q hq).hom` unfolds by `rfl` to `(…IsoPushforwardResolutionHomology …).hom ≫ (pushforwardIsoRightDerivedObj …).inv`, the proof becomes `exact paste_naturality_squares _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (sheafifiedLocalCohomologyIsoPushforwardResolutionHomology_hom_coefficient_naturality f a q hq) (pushforwardIsoRightDerivedObj_inv_coefficient_naturality f a q)` under a `show`/`change` to the composite form. The hypotheses are exactly the existing lemmas and the imports are unchanged.

Rewrite the first lemma. Use `h₁ := sheafifiedHPrimePushforwardResolutionHomologyPresheafIso_hom_coefficient_naturality f a q hq`. Use `h₂₃ := paste_naturality_squares _ _ _ _ _ _ _ (sheafifiedPushforwardResolutionMapHomologyIso_inv_coefficient_naturality f a q) (sheafifiedPushforwardResolutionComplexHomologyIso_hom_coefficient_naturality f a q)`, which is the square for `s.inv ≫ c.hom`. Then close with `paste_naturality_squares _ _ _ _ _ _ _ h₁ h₂₃`. This removes the `hcomp`, `h₂'`, `h₃'`, `h₁'`, `h₂''` and `e₁`/`e₂` chains.
findings.benefit: The proofs shrink from roughly 190 lines to about 10 each. The three- and two-square pastings read as direct applications of the already-stated component squares, so a reader sees which squares are glued. Future composite comparison isomorphisms, such as additional layers in this file, can reuse the lemma instead of writing another long term chain.
